title: The Parallel Wires
summary: Find the force between parallel currents, balance a floating wire and use the definition of the ampere.
subject: physics
ncertRef: Section 4.8, Force between two parallel currents, the ampere
concepts: Force on a loop near a wire
learningOutcome: The student can find the force between parallel currents and whether it attracts or repels, balance a wire against its weight, use the definition of the ampere, and add forces from several wires.

levels.title: Pull or push?
levels.adds: Baseline: F = (μ₀/2π) I₁I₂L/d, and parallel currents attract while antiparallel ones repel (Ex 4.7).
hints: F = 2 × 10⁻⁷ I₁I₂ L/d with the lengths in metres.
Give the force in µN: multiply the newtons by 10⁶.
Parallel currents attract, antiparallel currents repel.

levels.title: The floating wire
levels.adds: New idea: the repulsion between antiparallel wires can balance a weight (Section 4.8).
hints: Balance the repulsive force per metre against the weight per metre λg.
Closer than the balance, the force wins and the wire rises.

levels.title: The ampere
levels.adds: New idea: the ampere is defined through the force between wires, 2 × 10⁻⁷ N/m at 1 A and 1 m (Section 4.8).
hints: Doubling both currents multiplies the force by 2 × 2.

levels.title: Three wires
levels.adds: More steps: add the signed forces from two outer wires on the middle one.
hints: Take the direction towards wire 1 as positive.
A wire with a parallel current pulls the middle wire towards itself, an antiparallel one pushes it away.
Add the two as signed quantities, not as magnitudes.

levels.title: A loop near a wire
levels.adds: More steps: the near and far sides of a rectangular loop feel opposite forces, and the side arms cancel.
hints: The near side and the far side carry opposite currents and feel opposite forces.
The near side is closer, so its force is larger.
The side arms feel equal and opposite forces which cancel.

misconceptions: Parallel currents in the same direction repel
The force between two wires does not depend on both currents
Newton’s third law fails for the force between two wires
A loop next to a wire feels no net force
